newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk minster sees 1996 trade gap at $20 bln.
newsitem.headline: Turk minster sees 1996 trade gap at $20 bln.

text.p: Turkish State Minister Ayfer Yilmaz, in charge of foreign trade, said on Tuesday the 1996 trade deficit would stand at around $20 billion against a government target of $16 billion, state-owned Anatolian news agency reported.
She said imports were likely to hit $44 to $45 billion and exports $24-$25 billion this year, compared to official targets of $40 billion and $25 billion respectively.
"After looking at foreign trade data...we see that a deficit of about $20 billion may occur," the agency quoted Yilmaz as telling a business meeting in Istanbul.
She said Turkish exports could not take "the expected benefits from the customs union", an agreement with the European Union which took effect on January 1, 1996.
She blamed a high economic growth rate this year for boositng imports, especially those of investment goods.
According to the most recent official trade data, the deficit rose to $2.4 billion in January-February of this year, up 88.2 percent from the same 1995 period.
Turkish traders and industrialists forecast earlier that the deficit would rise up to $22 billion this year from $14 billion in 1995.
